stories.headline: Dream say concerns over finding available WNBA Finals venue went unheeded
stories.summary: In a letter to the city, the Atlanta Dream said Game 6 getting moved to 12:30 p.m. so they can play in State Farm Arena was "not what we fought for."
stories.body:
ATLANTA -- In an open letter addressed to the city, the Dream said concerns they had over the availability of a properly sized venue for WNBA Finals games in Atlanta went unheeded and that the solution of moving Game 6 up to 12:30 p.m. ET was "not what we fought for."

Game 6 between the Dream and Golden State Valkyries will be played Thursday at 12:30 p.m. as opposed to the original schedule of 8 p.m. The shift in timing was a result of the game being moved to State Farm Arena, the home of the Atlanta Hawks.

The Dream have played all of their home games this postseason at State Farm Arena, which seats roughly 17,000 fans. Their home court, Gateway Center, fits just 3,500.

To accommodate Game 6, the Hawks' home game against the Cleveland Cavaliers that night will move back one hour to 8 p.m., as was Game 4 at State Farm Arena. All three Finals games in Atlanta have required hurried adjustments to the schedule.

"As much as we have great affection and nostalgia for Gateway Center Arena, we believed that our fans and the city wanted the opportunity to be a part of this historic series, and to see it played on a world-class stage," the letter said. "That meant State Farm Arena."

According to the letter, the Dream brought up concerns the franchise had involving playoff scheduling and dates that overlapped with NBA games at the arena two months ago. The organization said it reiterated the issues as the playoffs went on but, "Our concerns did not receive the attention, nor the urgency that they deserved."

Multiple sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou that the dates for the 2026 playoffs were sent internally to teams on Dec. 4, 2025.

Negotiations between the WNBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, NBA and broadcast partners took place over the weekend to figure out the best course of action for all parties involved.

The NBA and WNBA explored options to keep Game 6 in primetime, ESPN's Ramona Shelbourne reported. However, the Hawks and Cavaliers both play Wednesday night, so they could not play their game in the earlier time slot Thursday.

"I hope everyone gets to see it somehow, and I know for some people it's not realistic -- they have jobs and won't be able to make it," Dream coach Karl Smesko said ahead of Game 5 in San Francisco. "I'm disappointed for that, but I'm hopeful as many people as possible can see the game."

In a statement Monday, WNBA commissioner Cathy Engelbert added: "The sellout crowds and extraordinary atmosphere at State Farm Arena for Games 3 and 4 were a tremendous success, and we're excited to give thousands more fans the opportunity to experience Game 6 with a championship on the line. We thank the NBA, Dream, Valkyries, Hawks, State Farm Arena and USA Network for the collaboration and flexibility that made this move possible. We look forward to delivering another unforgettable Finals experience in Atlanta."

Valkyries players Kiah Stokes and Veronica Burton encouraged fans in the Bay Area to call in sick to watch the game, while their coach, Natalie Nakase, expressed confidence that Golden State fans would tune in from wherever they had to despite the 9:30 a.m. tipoff in California.

Dream players including Allisha Gray, Jordin Canada and Angel Reese brushed aside the game time as a nonfactor.

"It's the Finals," Gray said. "We just got to do what we've got to do. We are locked in on winning Game 6 whether it's 8 a.m., 10 p.m., midnight. We got a championship to win."

stories.headline: Ayesha Curry to star in holiday rom-com 'Second Chance Holiday,' premiering on Roku
stories.summary: The wife of Stephen Curry will make her debut in a feature film leading role with Roku's "Second Chance Holiday."
stories.body:
Ayesha Curry is set to star in Roku's holiday rom-com, "Second Chance Holiday," premiering Nov. 5, Roku announced Tuesday. It marks Curry's debut in a feature film leading role.

Roku shared the news with a trailer that was released on social media. The channel first announced the movie in July with Curry, the wife of Golden State Warriors star Stephen, as the headliner. However, the trailer and release date weren't made available until Tuesday.

Ayesha will be starring alongside Matthew Daddario, the brother of movie star Alexandra.

"It's an honor to be part of Second Chance Holiday alongside such a talented cast and crew," Curry said in a July statement. "There's something truly magical about holiday rom-coms. They invite you into these charming, cozy worlds where anything feels possible. Chelsey is such a fun, heartfelt character that I fell in love with while bringing her to life. I hope audiences fall in love with her too and enjoy Second Chance Holiday this holiday season."

The film follows Curry as a dating expert looking to break a "curse" of frequently getting dumped during the holiday season, according to Roku. She is reunited with her high school crush, played by Daddario, and wonders if the bad luck is the universe's way of pushing her back to her first love.

Stephen and Ayesha have been married for 15 years and share four children together. The four-time NBA champion responded to the trailer on X, calling Ayesha his "leading lady."

Though Ayesha has never secured a leading film role, she has experience in front of the camera.

Her most recent role was in the animation movie "GOAT," which was produced by her husband, who also appeared in the movie. Ayesha has been credited for appearances in Disney's "Hannah Montana" and "Good Luck Charlie," plus HBO's "Ballers."

Now, she'll make her debut in a film set for the holidays that will stream on Roku.

stories.headline: World Series Game 4: Live updates from Brewers-Rays
stories.summary: The Fall Classic could end as soon as tonight with Milwaukee's first title. Here's the latest from the Trop.
stories.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers are just one win away from winning the 2026 World Series -- and the first title in franchise history.

In Game 3 on Monday night, the Brewers rode an eight-run fifth inning to a 10-1 victory over the Tamp Bay Rays. Now, Milwaukee has the chance to complete the sweep in Game 4 on Tuesday. Will the Brewers raise the trophy at Tropicana Field, or will the Rays keep their postseason alive and force a Game 5?

We've got you covered with keys to the matchup and pregame lineups -- and stay tuned for in-game action and postgame takeaways from Tampa Bay.

Key links: How to win World Series | Playoff MVP tracker | Full schedule

Live updates

Milwaukee Brewers at Tampa Bay Rays (8 p.m. ET)
Starting pitchers: Dustin May vs. Griffin Jax

How the Brewers can finish it off: Don't change a thing. The Brewers are hitting with purpose, fielding with confidence and pitching with vigor. They can smell their first World Series title. And with a bullpen game scheduled and all of Milwaukee's leverage relief arms working on at least two days' rest, Pat Murphy will strategically deploy his surfeit of relievers to exploit the best matchups. Should the Brewers chase Rays starter Jax early, Tampa Bay's bullpen hasn't shown much ability to lock down Milwaukee's hitters, another checkmark in Milwaukee's favor. Everything has been good so far this series, leading the Brewers to wonder, with good reason: Why would anything change now?

How the Rays can stay alive: Treat every at-bat like their season depends on it. (Because it does.) Generate swings and misses. (Which Jax is capable of doing.) Play their best players. (A day after sitting Jonathan Aranda and Liam Hicks for platoon reasons.) Get back to playing Rays baseball. (Clean, fun, focused.) More than anything, remind themselves that they won 98 games and romped through the American League bracket and that these last three games are not a reflection of who this team is. Bad stretches happen, and it's a shame when they happen in the first three games of the World Series, and, sure, no team ever has come back from a 3-0 deficit and won. But history can only be made one out at a time, and securing 27 is the first step. -- Jeff Passan

stories.headline: NFL trade deadline grades: DeForest Buckner, Quenton Nelson dealt by Colts, more
stories.summary: Does Buckner make the 49ers Super Bowl hopefuls? Will Quenton Nelson upgrade the Seahawks' O-line? We're grading NFL trades ahead of November's deadline.
stories.body:
NFL analysts Ben Solak and Seth Walder are grading deals ahead of the 2026 trade deadline, which is Nov. 10 at 4 p.m. ET.

When grading trades, we evaluate them for each team based on on-field impact, cap implications, draft compensation and effects within the context of a team's overall short- and long-term outlooks. How confident are we in knowing if this is a good or bad decision? And how big is the impact of this decision? Both questions play a role in our grades, though a low-impact decision can still receive a strong or poor grade. Even with lower stakes, clear-cut wins or losses still matter.

Here are our evaluations for the first deals of trading season, including the Colts sending guard Quenton Nelson to Seattle and defensive tackle DeForest Buckner to San Francisco. Check back through the deadline for grades on the biggest moves.

Jump to a trade:

Buckner | Nelson | Harrison

Jurgens | Porter | McCarthy

Colts trade DT Buckner to 49ers

49ers get: DT DeForest Buckner

Colts get: 2027 fourth-round pick

49ers grade: A-

Colts grade: B-

As soon as the Colts emerged as a team that might engage in a trade-deadline teardown, it wasn't hard to see the dots connecting Buckner back to the 49ers. That became a reality Tuesday.

Though his numbers have dipped, Buckner, 32, can still help the 49ers get after the quarterback. He has four sacks this season, but his pass rush win rate ranked in the 45th percentile among defensive tackles, alongside a 69th percentile pressure rate. That is a drop from last season, when he was in the 90th and 88th percentile in those metrics, respectively. However, that 2025 performance is a positive sign for what he could bring to the 49ers the rest of this season.

Extra pass-rushing help will be welcome in San Francisco, which ranks 19th in pass rush win rate. The 49ers have been without Nick Bosa, who has been out because of a calf injury since Week 3 but is expected to return soon. Their pass defense is the only one of their major units (run and pass on offense and defense) that ranks outside the top seven in EPA per play (13th).

I'll admit I'm a little surprised the 49ers made this move considering they already have Osa Odighizuwa as a pass-rush-first defensive tackle. But he can play next to Buckner -- especially on passing downs. Also, San Francisco's rash of defensive line injuries makes any help welcome.

This type of roster-bolstering move makes sense for San Francisco. The 49ers are the Super Bowl favorites, according to ESPN's Football Power Index. In fact, they are the favorites by a lot, with the FPI giving them a 23% chance to win the Super Bowl (every other team is below 11%). Adding Buckner to reinforce those chances is worthwhile.

The cost was also quite reasonable. The 49ers are surrendering a fourth-round pick and taking over the prorated remainder of Buckner's $13 million salary, assuming his contract is untouched. While compensatory picks are never a guarantee, there's a decent chance that San Francisco might recoup most of that draft capital back via a comp pick if Buckner signs elsewhere in free agency next offseason, especially given that San Francisco is low on 2027 cap space.

That also is why I'm a little critical of the Colts' move here. Don't get me wrong, it absolutely makes sense for Indianapolis to trade him. The Colts are rebuilding, and Buckner is a 32-year-old in the final year of his contract -- of course they should have dealt him before the deadline.

Perhaps this was the best offer Indianapolis received for Buckner today, but they also didn't have to trade Buckner right now. There are two weeks left until the Nov. 10 trade deadline. I would have thought they could have at least squeezed another Day 3 pick in addition to the fourth-rounder. -- Walder

Colts trade G Nelson to Seahawks
Seahawks get: G Quenton Nelson

Colts get: 2027 third-round pick, 2028 fifth-round pick

Seahawks grade: A-

Colts grade: B+

The reimagination of the Colts is officially underway, with longtime Indianapolis stalwart Nelson heading to the defending Super Bowl champions to bolster the interior of their offensive line.

Nelson, 30, started his career with three consecutive first-team All-Pro selections. His level of play dropped in 2022 and 2023, but the 2018 first-round pick battled back to elite form in 2024, when he posted pass block and run block win rates that were each in the 90th percentile, along with earning second-team All-Pro honors. He earned a second-team All-Pro spot last season, too, along with a 91st percentile and 74th percentile pass block and run block win rates, respectively.

His win rates haven't been quite as strong this season (66th and 37th percentile, respectively), but Nelson's reputation is still superb, and having such consistent results the previous two years suggests he probably remains one of the best guards in the league if we're projecting the rest of the season.

The Seahawks presumably will keep Nelson at left guard and move Grey Zabel to right guard. That will push Anthony Bradford, who recently returned from injured reserve and has played two games this season, to the bench. Bradford recorded 30th and 33rd percentile pass block and run block win rates last season, respectively, so Nelson is a substantial upgrade.

The Seahawks have Super Bowl aspirations but must get better play out of an offense that ranks 26th in EPA per play and 31st in EPA per designed rush. They rank 27th in run block win rate, 28th in yards per designed running back carry (3.6) and 28th in yards before contact on designed run plays. They also rank 21st in pass block win rate. So the team needed some offensive line help and upgrading their right guard or center made sense.

Nelson is on an expiring contract, so unless his deal was altered, the Seahawks will take on the prorated remainder of his $16 million in salary for this season, which is a bargain for the quality of play he brings. The Seahawks could sign Nelson to an extension or a new deal after the season, but they could also let him walk in free agency and possibly collect a compensatory pick to mitigate the draft capital lost in this trade.

It makes a lot of sense for the Seahawks to push their chips in on their current team. History tells us how hard it is to sustain elite defensive success, so the Seahawks need to take advantage while they have it.

This was also an easily logical move for the Colts. The 2026 season is lost, and Nelson is a pending free agent. Whatever value he would bring to the team in the second half of the season pales in comparison to what he brings to the Seahawks, and the draft capital return is more than they would get in compensatory picks (which are never a guarantee, anyway) had Nelson left in free agency. Plus, they save money on the remainder of his 2026 salary.

Ultimately, this is a win-win trade. Considering Seattle's contention window, positional (and overall offensive) need, the draft capital required and Nelson's contract, this is a sound move. -- Walder

Cardinals trade WR Harrison Jr. to Texans
Texans get: WR Marvin Harrison Jr., 2027 seventh-round pick

Cardinals get: 2027 second-round pick, 2027 sixth-round pick

Texans grade: C+

Cardinals: A-

Minutes after the Texans completed their 26-3 blowout win over the Titans, news broke that the rumored trade of Harrison, who was inactive Sunday because of the expected move, would be completed. The Cardinals sent him to Houston for a second-rounder and a sixth-rounder in 2027.

Similar to a lot of trades for young players, there are two simple questions: How much of our opinion of Harrison should be shaped by the league's predraft opinion of him and how much should be based on what we've seen from him in the NFL so far?

Harrison was considered a premier wide receiver prospect and was the first non-quarterback off the board with the fourth pick in the 2024 draft. But his production has fallen well short of those expectations to date, with Harrison amassing 1,578 receiving yards over 33 career games.

That equates to 1.5 yards per route run, which is in the 46th percentile among wide receivers who have run at least 15 routes per team game in that span. That number has been even worse in a small sample this season: just 0.6 yards per route run with a much higher percentage of deep fades and go routes (24%) than the previous two seasons (13%). Harrison's player-tracking metrics have been mediocre but not awful during his first two seasons: 47 and 54 overall in ESPN's receiver scores (with slightly better open scores) in 2024 and 2025, respectively.

Despite a rough start, the 1-4 Texans probably still believe they have a Super Bowl-caliber defense and a chance for a postseason run if they can get more talent around quarterback C.J. Stroud, who has been playing well. I don't think that's far-fetched despite their record. This is not the Texans' first attempt to upgrade at wide receiver. After second-year man Jayden Higgins suffered a torn ACL in August, Houston acquired Kayshon Boutte from the Patriots. But Boutte has managed only 1.1 yards per route run despite Nico Collins missing two games.

The Texans will get Harrison for cheap for the rest of this season and next year, and they will have a fifth-year option on him for 2028. But this move is not worth it if Harrison remains the same player he has been with the Cardinals because second-round picks have real value. Receivers who average 1.5 yards per route run can be found quite easily. The Texans are betting that Harrison can reach the upside he showed at Ohio State, including a breakout season in 2022 when Stroud was his quarterback. Having already played two-plus NFL seasons, the chances of a breakout aren't great, but they exist.

I think this trade makes sense for Arizona. The Cardinals didn't have to trade Harrison yet, but he will be worth more to a contending team than he is to them. It's likely his trade value would sink if they waited until the offseason to deal him. And Michael Wilson already had established himself as Arizona's No. 1 receiver.

Ultimately, I would not have made this trade if I were the Texans because the odds of Harrison breaking out immediately feel too low to justify the compensation. But I at least understand the thought process and desire to maximize a loaded roster's chances of making a real run to make the playoffs and win postseason games. -- Walder

Eagles trade C Jurgens to Ravens
Ravens get: C Cam Jurgens, 2027 seventh-round pick

Eagles get: 2027 fifth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Ravens grade: D+

Eagles grade: A

First, Tyler Linderbaum walked in free agency. Then the Ravens lost Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic to injury, suddenly leaving them without a center. Last week, Baltimore moved first-round rookie guard Olaivavega Ioane to center but evidently doesn't see that as a long-term option.

So Baltimore turned to the trade market and dealt for Jurgens. It's an interesting and unusual move, because Jurgens is no stopgap. He's only 27 years old and is already on a long-term deal after signing an extension with the Eagles in 2025.

Jurgens moved from center to left guard in Week 2 after the Eagles placed guard Landon Dickerson on injured reserve. It has not gone well. Jurgens ranks in the bottom three in both pass block and run block win rate at guard. But the Ravens are trading for Jurgens to have him play center.

In 2024, Jurgens was a Pro Bowl center who recorded pass block and run block win rates in the 80th and 50th percentiles, respectively. He made the Pro Bowl again in 2025, but his numbers slipped to the 65th and 39th percentile, respectively. He should be a stabilizing force for the Ravens -- perhaps an average to above-average center -- at what has suddenly become a position of need. But the cost is exorbitant.

The Ravens are surrendering a second-round pick (plus a swap of fifth- and seventh-round picks) for the right to pay a non-premium position player market price after this season. Jurgens is due a fully guaranteed $16 million next year. He's due $17 million (non-guaranteed) in 2028 and 2029. Jurgens' $17 million average per year for the duration of his contract makes him the fourth-highest-paid center in the league, behind only Linderbaum, Creed Humphrey and Aaron Brewer, per OverTheCap.com. By comparison, Connor McGovern, who had better numbers than Jurgens last season, makes a little over $13 million per year.

One saving grace for Baltimore is that Jurgens' salary is cheap this season. The Eagles have already paid Jurgens' option bonus, so the Ravens should be on the hook for only the remaining portion of his $1.2 million base salary.

For the Eagles, the loss of Jurgens is the latest blow to an offensive line that is already down Dickerson and recently retired tackle Lane Johnson. Jurgens hadn't played well at guard, but surely they saw him as their long-term center. Drew Kendall, who has played center after Jurgens' shift, has been below average in both pass and run block win rate this season. But the Eagles seemed to believe this was a price too good to pass up.

I understand that the Ravens rightfully believe they are Super Bowl contenders, probably want Ioane to stay and develop at guard and thought they needed to fill their gap at center. Making a trade before the deadline to fix that issue makes sense. But almost certainly there would have been cheaper options out there than this. And the timing is odd, considering that Jurgens is currently in concussion protocol and not expected to play Sunday.

So it seems like the Eagles sensed Baltimore's desperation and squeezed an overpay out of the Ravens. -- Walder

Steelers trade CB Porter to Cowboys
Cowboys get: CB Joey Porter Jr.

Steelers get: 2027 sixth-round pick, 2028 second-round pick

Cowboys grade: B

Steelers grade: C+

This is the Cowboys' third trade with the Steelers in the past 18 months (George Pickens and Broderick Jones), and it's their third trade involving a star defensive player after acquiring Quinnen Williams at the trade deadline last season and shipping Micah Parsons to Green Bay last offseason.

It's easy to see what the Cowboys are doing here. DaRon Bland, who first broke onto the scene as a slot corner, was playing on the outside given Dallas' lack of depth. By acquiring Porter, Bland can move back inside, which will allow the Cowboys to relocate 2026 first-round defensive back Caleb Downs, as well. He has been playing the slot, but his natural position is at safety. These are options, not guarantees. Bland might stay outside as the Cowboys instead pursue a strong 1-2 punch at outside corner, with Porter shadowing WR1s.

The salient point is this: Porter can have a rising tide impact on the Cowboys secondary, clarifying the roles of other players and enhancing the whole unit in the process.

Porter is not as tricky of a scheme fit in Dallas as people think, too. His strengths are certainly his length and physicality, such that he can line up in press -- but he has been in press alignments on only 30.6% of his snaps over his career, just above the league average for cornerbacks (24.1%). Porter is a much better man coverage defender than he is in zone, as his passer rating allowed in man coverage over the past four seasons is better than all but Derek Stingley Jr. But the Cowboys are actually running more man coverage (24.8%) under first-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker than the league average (23.2%) over the first three weeks.

Of course, early-season rate stats can be noisy. Parker's Vic Fangio-inspired defense will require Porter to play from greater depth than he did in Pittsburgh, and the communication and keys required in that match-heavy system will take some getting used to. But Porter has a valuable and rare skill set in his press-man ability, and premium picks should be spent on players with premium traits. The Cowboys got much, much better in the secondary -- though the move is not without risk.

Acquiring Porter does not solve all their deficiencies; linebacker is still a big problem for this team, and the edge rush isn't far behind. But if the secondary needs less schematic help now that Porter is in play, more coaching tools can be used to hide those other weak spots.

For the Steelers, Porter's recurring back ailments seemed incurable without an extension or a relocation -- what can you do? It's frustrating that GM Omar Khan invested more in third-contract players like Jalen Ramsey and T.J. Watt over a younger, second-contract player like Porter -- Ramsey and Watt will hit their athletic wall far sooner than Porter. Jamel Dean, another third-contract player signed to play corner opposite Porter, now has to cover WR1s alongside Asante Samuel Jr. and 2026 third-round pick Daylen Everette. Corner is no longer a strong position on Pittsburgh's depth chart.

Porter reportedly had contract demands up at the top of the cornerback market, where Devon Witherspoon and Christian Gonzalez recently reset elite deals to clear $33 million annually. I'm not sold that Porter is a top-tier corner deserving of that top money. But because the Steelers let this go on for so long and bleed into the regular season, they were only able to acquire a 2027 sixth-round pick and a 2028 second-round pick for a young, ascendent cover corner. They could have -- and should have -- gotten at least a first-round pick by playing this differently and dealing Porter in the spring or earlier in the summer. -- Solak

Vikings trade QB McCarthy to Giants
Giants get: QB J.J. McCarthy

Vikings get: 2027 fifth-round pick

Giants grade: C

Vikings grade: B+

A mere 22 days after the Giants signed Jameis Winston to a two-year, $13 million extension, New York decided it needed to trade a fifth-round pick for an alternative at quarterback. Of course, a lot has happened in three weeks.

Starting quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury in Week 2 that is expected to keep him out for at least the regular season. And Winston has delivered two poor performances in Dart's stead, with a 19.0 QBR in relief in Week 2 against the Rams and a 27.9 in Sunday's 12-7 win over the Titans. So in comes McCarthy, the No. 10 pick in the 2024 draft.

McCarthy's pro career has gone poorly so far, which is putting it mildly. He suffered a season-ending knee injury in August 2024, which helped Sam Darnold become Minnesota's starting quarterback. McCarthy was named the starter last season after Darnold departed in free agency but started only 10 games after a series of injuries cost him time. And when he was on the field, the results were not good.

McCarthy posted a 36.1 QBR in 2025 (which ranked 38th out of 45 quarterbacks with at least 100 pass attempts) and recorded a minus-5% pass rate over expected, per NFL Next Gen Stats (43rd out of 45). He threw interceptions at a 4.2% clip (44th), took sacks on 9.4% of dropbacks (40th) and had a 1.8% fumble rate (41st). More alarming is that he did all that while playing for Kevin O'Connell, who has seemingly elevated most of the non-McCarthy quarterbacks he has called plays for.

During training camp, not only did McCarthy lose the Vikings' starting quarterback competition to Kyler Murray, but he then lost the backup competition to Carson Wentz, too. That is a telling red flag.

So why would the Giants trade for him? McCarthy presumably still has some upside based on his draft pedigree, and the Giants are hoping they can profit from him realizing it. But it's hard not to notice the fact that this is John Harbaugh trading for the quarterback his brother, Jim Harbaugh, coached in college at Michigan.

It is difficult to know from the outside which other backup quarterbacks would have been available, but McCarthy still does not seem like an ideal choice. Mac Jones and Spencer Rattler ought to have been the team's first calls (maybe they were). Kirk Cousins probably is off the board with the Raiders sitting at 3-0. Mitchell Trubisky might have been available, considering this already looks like a lost season for Tennessee. And I'm assuming Gardner Minshew II surely must be available, considering he sits in veteran no-man's land between Jacoby Brissett and rookie Carson Beck in Arizona. Stetson Bennett IV could have been an option, too, after the Rams selected Ty Simpson in the first round of this year's draft. I'll grant that some of those options have less upside than McCarthy.

But the Giants' front office should look in the mirror over its bungling of the Winston situation. It's not unreasonable for the Giants to be aggressive in finding a better replacement given how much time is left in the season. But they clearly shouldn't have signed Winston to an extension right before the season if this is how they feel about him!

Even though Murray is a free agent at the end of this season, McCarthy's ship had already sailed in Minnesota after he couldn't beat out Wentz. If he wasn't going to be the Vikings' backup quarterback, his value would likely have continued to drop. To get a fifth-round pick while saving a few million across his remaining 2026 and 2027 compensation (not nothing!) makes sense. They have uncertainty at quarterback in 2027, yes. But that was true whether McCarthy was there or not. -- Walder

stories.headline: Salkilld, Saint Denis to headline UFC Fight Night in Sydney
stories.summary: West Australian Quillan Salkilld will headline a UFC Fight Night lightweight matchup with Benoît Saint Denis in Sydney in February.
stories.body:
West Australian Quillan Salkilld will return to the Octagon in Sydney, after it was confirmed he'll headline the UFC Fight Night with a lightweight bout against Frenchman Benoît Saint Denis on February 7 (AEDT).

Salkilld, 26, is a former Australian rules footballer who turned to MMA after leaving school at 16, and boasts an impressive 13-1 professional record (6-0 in UFC) with five 'performance of the night' bonuses.

The Broome native has won four consecutive fights with a first-round finish, most recently submitting Mateusz Gamrot in their UFC Fight Night clash in Perth in August. He's widely regarded as Australia's next big combat star.

Meanwhile Saint Denis, 30, is one of the lightweight division's most dangerous finishers, and has a 17-4 professional record.

Peter Kloczko, senior vice president of UFC Australia and New Zealand, said the Fight Night -- to take place at Sydney's Afterpay Arena -- would be an "unforgettable event" featuring one of Australia's brightest young stars.

"UFC Fight Night Sydney is set to be another huge moment for Australian fans, and Quillan Salkilld versus Benoît Saint Denis is a main event that delivers everything we look for in this sport," he said in the official release.

"Quillan has been one of the breakout stars of the UFC's lightweight division, while Benoît is one of the most dangerous and exciting finishers in the sport. Bringing this fight to Sydney will make for an unforgettable night."

Further fights on the card will be released in due course.

stories.headline: Is Fleetwood Town's defeat of Arsenal the biggest upset in League Cup history?
stories.summary: Arsenal aren't the only Premier League side to suffer Cup humiliation; ESPN takes a look at all the famous "giant killings" in England's League Cup.
stories.body:
(Editor's note: This article was originally published in 2025 and has been updated following Fleetwood Town's triumph on Tuesday.)

A case can be made that Fleetwood Town's shock penalty shootout win over Arsenal is the biggest upset in League Cup history.

There have been plenty of remarkable boilovers through the years, so it's got competition, but the Gunners entered Tuesday evening's contest as the reigning Premier League champions and with just one loss across 11 league and UEFA Champions League fixtures this season.

Mikel Arteta's side fell behind in the 21st minute when Aaron Loupalo-Bi shook off the attention of Marli Salmon and fired an effort through the legs of keeper Illan Meslier. And while Viktor Gyökeres would pull the visitors back level five minutes into the second stanza and they would dominate possession, the Premier League giants couldn't find a winner inside 90 minutes - forcing the game to penalties.

- Hunter: If the Clásico is any indication, Mou's Madrid might be special again

- Ranked: Every Premier League team's money-per-points (after City cheated)

- Jones: Vozinha's Ballon d'Or night a perfect moment for soccer's dreamers

Both sides were perfect from the spot until Bruno Guimarães -- just months on from missing a penalty that would have put Brazil 1-0 up in their eventual round of 16 loss to Norway at the FIFA World Cup -- was denied by Fleetwood custodian Jay Lynch.

Teenage defender Conor Haughey then smashed home the winning penalty to spark a pitch invasion as the Cod Army knocked off a side 84 places above them in the English pyramid and claimed possibly the greatest win in their history.

"We talked about Grimsby beating Man United last year; we compared it, even though these are the champions, and thought, if we gave it a go, let's see what happens," Lynch told Sky. "It's amazing for the club, for the club, it means everything to everyone."

It was an evening tinged by a level of madness of all sorts: 16-year-old Max Dowman sent off in the 85th minute after lashing out following a physical challenge from Harrison Neal and play suspended for eight minutes after a drone was flown above the pitch in just the second minute.

"I'm gonna be honest, we haven't practiced once, in terms of penalties," Fleetwood boss Matt Lawlor told Sky. "I'm not gonna sit here and blag you and say we've done some meticulous penalties; we haven't practiced."

It's a result that slots comfortably into ESPN's stockpile of giant killings in the League Cup.

2025 -- Grimsby Town 2-2 Manchester United (12-11 on penalties)

Manchester United hit new depths when they were bundled out of the second round of the League Cup by League Two outfit Grimsby Town in 2025 -- their first ever cup elimination from a side in England's fourth tier.

Down 2-0 at half-time thanks to goals from Charles Vernam and Tyrell Warren, United avoided the ignominy of a regular-time defeat when Bryan Mbeumo and Harry Maguire dragged the game back to parity -- the latter netting his equaliser in the 89th minute -- but then fell after a mammoth penalty shootout.

Then-boss Ruben Amorim apologised to supporters after the game, and he himself became the subject of internet ridicule when footage of him adjusting his tactics board in driving rain was shown on the broadcast, as his side, worth hundreds of millions of pounds, were down 2-0 to a League Two side.

2006 -- Southend United 1-0 Manchester United
Cristiano Ronaldo, Wayne Rooney and Patrice Evra were all on the pitch as holders Man United fell to a fourth-round League Cup exit to Championship strugglers Southend.

A 30-yard free-kick from Freddie Eastwood -- who played 11 times for Wales -- secured the win for Southend against Sir Alex Ferguson's United side that contained 10 internationals.

United went on to win the Premier League that season.

2010 -- Liverpool 2-2 Northampton Town (2-4 on penalties)

League Two Northampton Town completed a scarcely believable upset at Anfield in the third round of the League Cup in 2010.

Milan Jovanovic put Liverpool infront inside ten minutes before Billy McKay and Michael Jacobs put Northampton a goal to the good at 2-1.

David N'Gog scored an equaliser late in extra-time for Liverpool to take the game to penalties where Abdul Osman put away the decisive spot-kick to hand Liverpool -- under Roy Hodgson at the time -- one of their worst ever home defeats.

2012 -- Bradford City 1-1 Arsenal (3-2 on penalties)
Another League Two side -- Bradford City -- dumped out top Premier league opposition in the League Cup quarterfinal in 2012 after beating Arsenal on penalties.

Garry Thomspon put Bradford ahead before Thomas Vermaelen scored in the 88th minute to take a full-strength Arsenal side to extra-time and an eventual penalty shootout against fourth-tier Bradford.

Jack Wilshere and Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain scored their penalties but misses from Santi Cazorla and Vermaelen sent Bradford through.

Current Wrexham manager Phil Parkinson, then of Bradford, went on to lead the side to the final of the competition that year, falling to a 5-0 defeat against Swansea City at Wembley.

2014 -- MK Dons 4-0 Manchester United

Perhaps the most shocking defeat of this list came in 2014 when Louis Van Gaal's Man United were thrashed 4-0 by League One MK Dons in the second-round of the League Cup -- the last time they exited at that stage before their defeat to Grimsby.

Will Grigg and Arsenal loanee Benik Afobe both scored braces at Stadium MK on the way to an untroubled victory for MK Dons against a United team featuring the likes of David De Gea, Jonny Evans and Javier Hernández.

2019 -- Colchester United 0-0 Tottenham Hotspur (4-3 on penalties)
Mauricio Pochettino's Tottenham exited the 2019 Carabao Cup at the third-round courtesy of League Two Colchester -- the lowest ranked side left in the competition.

Christian Eriksen, Dele Alli, Lucas Moura and Son Heung-Min couldn't break down a resolute Colchester as the game went to penalties.

Tom Lapslie scored the winning spot-kick in the shootout after Eriksen and Moura missed for Spurs sending Colchester into the League Cup last 16 for the first time in 44 years.

2019 -- Oxford United 4-0 West Ham
Oxford United manager Karl Robinson called his side's 4-0 victory over West Ham in the third round of the League Cup in 2019, one of the biggest results in the club's history.

Goals from Elliot Moore, Matt Taylor, Tarique Fosu-Henry and Shandon Baptiste gave Oxford the win at the Kassam Stadium over Manuel Pellegrini's West Ham team that started with 10 full internationals.

The match was the second major cup upset Jack Wilshere, who started in midfield, was involved in. He had also started for Arsenal in their defeat to Bradford in the same competition seven years earlier.

stories.headline: Power to burn and a 'trademark' goal: why Ethan Drever has rocketed up draft boards
stories.summary: Growing up an Essendon supporter, Ethan Drever hasn't 'seen anything' like success. But his rise up draft boards could have him in the frame to be his childhood club's first pick, writes Jasper Chellappah.
stories.body:
Ethan Drever had absolutely no choice on his AFL team. As a newborn he was put in an Essendon jumper at the hospital and he's been a Bomber ever since.

It's been a rough 18 years of fandom since, and he's got some thoughts about his dad's decision.

"I'm [born in] 2008, I haven't seen anything!" he tells ESPN with a grin - and a grimace.

"Dad tells me about his success and I'm like, 'You don't have to rub it in like that.'"

The Dons are entering a new era in 2027 under Mark McVeigh and it's being driven through the draft. They snagged Sullivan Robey, Jacob Farrow, and Dyson Sharp in the first round 12 months ago and now own pick 1 in the upcoming draft.

Drever also has a lot of thoughts about those drafted before him.

"They've got some good young boys in there now. Robey, Sharp, they're gonna be so good.

"I like Farrow. He should be kicking in and doing all that, he needs to be in priority positions. That's what he's gonna be doing in the future.

"Just that halfback, I reckon he's gonna be really good... he's a beautiful left foot kick."

After a dour two-win season the Bombers have first call on Drever, with the 188cm on-baller strongly linked at the top of the board.

He's an electric runner with the intent to tackle, chase, and pressure - something that hasn't been a trait of Essendon's list for a long time.

Asked what he thinks when watching his boyhood club each weekend, Drever's response would prick the ears of all Bombers fans.

"It'd be nice to be out there and sort of help the boys out, that's kinda what I'm thinking!"

The Vic Country MVP and Rebels best and fairest produced a remarkable season. His star has risen from a first-round chance to the very top of the open pool.

He may have the most translatable traits to AFL level of any prospect. Drever is an elite power athlete, recording a 2.92 second 20 metre sprint which comes across in the tape. He bursts out of the contest with driving legs and loves to exit forward of the stoppage to inflict maximum damage.

His ultra consistent season has come about without any injury concerns, something all other top prospects this year haven't been able to say.

"It's been good not to have to sit on the sidelines this year at all and I can just keep playing consistent footy," he says.

"I only missed one [game] which was just after champs, I just had a break."

Drever lays claim to a pretty handy trademark. On six separate occasions this season he's collected the ball -- either out of a stoppage or in open play -- and powered away from opponents into the forward half of the ground.

From there his long running gait and elite top speed helps him separate from chasing defenders and break the paint of 50 to drive home sensational goals.

"I have heard it's called the trademark goal now. I don't know where that's really come from, it's just a natural thing I guess. I just like to run and have a ping from outside 50," Drever tells ESPN.

"Definitely one of my traits is just my power, especially this year. Building up over the pre-season and definitely my two-way running.

"It's the long-term goal to move into the midfield and be a bit of a Jordan Dawson with his two-way running. I love Finn Callaghan, how he plays. Those two are really great role models for me.

"I think Hugh McCluggage as well, I've watched him a lot. I had a meeting with him this year, he's that sort of two-way runner as well and he's been really good for me."

Drever played 13 games for the Rebels this year in amongst commitments with the AFL Academy and Vic Country. He collected the ball 28 times to go with a goal a game, but he's not satisfied with just being an offensive weapon.

The Ballarat local is a tenacious presence in contests with the appetite to chase and tackle, racking up 6.5 per outing to frank his status as the best pure midfielder in the open pool.

At the draft combine he showed off a much-improved engine running a 6:27 minute 2km after going 20 seconds slower in the lead-up. It's a time that will put him towards the front of the pack on day one of pre-season.

Drever knows exactly what's required to be a midfielder at the next level, and he's determined to get there as soon as possible.

"My endurance side was a big goal of mine, obviously at the top level you've just got to be able to run all day.

"Honing in on my fundamentals and trying to get them the best I can as well. That's what the most important thing is because it's the little one percenters that make a difference in the AFL.

Drever is now on the precipice of living out his dream of becoming an AFL player, and it could be for his boyhood club as the top choice in the open pool of the draft.

That won't matter to him, so long as he gets his opportunity to shine on the big stage.

"I don't really care [if I go at pick 1]. It's nice to have my name up in consideration alongside those boys but I'll just be happy to be picked up wherever I go."

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey players to add: Goalie tandems, third skaters from top lines

Fantasy points don't happen in a vacuum. This week, we're looking at something a box score can't show you: the fantasy points a forward line scores at 5-on-5 only when all three players are on the ice together, including points by the defenders on the ice with them.

No line comes close to Colorado's rate, and it explains Lehkonen's 14th-place ranking among forwards: 16.0 of his 33.8 fantasy points have come with MacKinnon and Necas at 5-on-5 alone. Podkolzin's 13.8 with McDavid and Draisaitl is 40% of his total. Last week we called both passengers. This is what the passenger seat looks like.

The more useful finds are further down the list, where a few lines are producing with players nobody has rostered:

Kaapo Kakko, Shane Wright and Berkly Catton, Seattle Kraken (available in 96%, 99% and 98.3%): 44.6 FP in 82 minutes, the third-best rate at 5.43 per 10 minutes. Catton has scored more than half of his fantasy points with this line, and all three went back onto Seattle's top power-play unit Saturday.

Jaden Schwartz, Fedor Svechkov and T.J. Hughes, Colorado Avalanche (Schwartz available in 91.0%, Hughes in 98.5%): 39.4 FP in 72 minutes, the second-best rate at 5.51 per 10 minutes. Schwartz and Hughes are also on Colorado's top power-play unit.

He isn't on either power-play unit, but his 46 hits give him a floor in leagues that count them.

Alex DeBrincat, Emmitt Finnie and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard, Detroit Red Wings (Finnie available in 92.4%, Brandsegg-Nygard in 87.2%): 42.8 FP in 79 minutes (5.42 per 10 minutes), with the two kids splitting their share almost evenly.

Jack Quinn, Noah Ostlund and Zach Benson, Buffalo Sabres (Ostlund available in 96.6%, Benson in 88.2%): 45.4 FP in 115 minutes (3.95 per 10 minutes). The trio also stays together on the Sabres' top power-play unit with Tage Thompson and Rasmus Dahlin. Ostlund and Benson each play more than 80 percent of the team's power-play time at about four minutes a night, so the role is bigger than their FPPG suggests.

Frederick Gaudreau, Ryan Winterton and Ben Meyers, Seattle Kraken (Gaudreau available in 84.0%): 38.9 FP in 77 minutes (5.07 per 10 minutes). It's a deep-league play, but a fourth line producing like this is rare. Gaudreau and his six goals are the short-term target.

stories.headline: Lens fans banned from Liverpool match for throwing flares vs. Brugge
stories.summary: Fans of Ligue 1 club Lens were banned from buying tickets for a Champions League game at Liverpool by a UEFA disciplinary ruling Tuesday.
stories.body:
NYON, Switzerland -- Fans of Ligue 1 club Lens were banned from buying tickets for a Champions League game at Liverpool by a UEFA disciplinary ruling on Tuesday.

Lens fans lit dozens of flares and threw some toward rival supporters and the field, forcing the team's Champions League game at Club Brugge last week to be stopped briefly. Lens lost 3-0.

The club already were on probation by UEFA for fans lighting flares and fireworks at a previous Champions League game at Slavia Prague in September.

UEFA said its appeals judges imposed a ban on Lens selling tickets to fans for two Champions League away games.

The sanction will be served when Lens play at Leipzig on Nov. 24 and at Liverpool at Anfield on Jan. 27. A third game ban is deferred for a two-year probationary period.

UEFA said Lens were fined €80,000 ($89,000) for charges of "lighting and throwing of pyrotechnics as well as for acts of damage."

stories.headline: A benchmark for modern F1 circuits, eyesores and aching backs: The contradictions of Austin's COTA
stories.summary: The United States Grand Prix is well-loved by fans and drivers, but there were mixed reviews coming out of the weekend.
stories.body:
Ask Lewis Hamilton, and he'll tell you Austin's Circuit of the Americas is one of the best venues in sport. Ask Carlos Sainz, and he'll tell you the circuit is the blueprint for what a modern Formula 1 racetrack should look like. Ask Max Verstappen, and he might suggest COTA's boss would struggle to walk if he did five laps of the track.

The contrasting assessments reflect the sometimes bumpy reality of running one of Formula 1's most successful events. Fourteen years after Formula 1 first arrived in the Texas capital, the United States Grand Prix is enjoying another monumental commercial success: ahead of Sunday's race, F1 confirmed a record 467,000 fans had attended across the race weekend. Remarkably, circuit boss Bobby Epstein believes the sprawling venue could have accommodated considerably more than its new record figure, and comfortably so.

While Miami and Las Vegas have brought F1's American boom to new audiences, neither's arrival has displaced Austin's reputation as a favourite among drivers and fans alike. Its appeal has always been relatively straightforward: a proper racetrack, enormous crowds and a festival atmosphere that stretches far beyond what happens on the asphalt.

But as Formula 1 has grown, so has the event around it, something which was more apparent than ever before this year. From record attendances to an enormous (and much-debated) new luxury clubhouse overlooking Turn 1, COTA is facing the same challenge confronting circuits across the calendar: how to embrace the extraordinary commercial success of modern F1 without losing the things that made it special in the first place.

"That's why we stopped selling tickets," Epstein told ESPN. "Our biggest boundary that holds us back right now are the roads that access the facility, which are scheduled to be greatly expanded within two years. And I think when that does, we should pass the half-million mark on weekend attendance.

- F1 readies Antonelli's title champagne in Austin: 'The race of a champion who isn't champion yet'

- How Kimi Antonelli can win F1 title at Mexico City GP -- with or without Qatar, Abu Dhabi races

- Max Verstappen taking painkillers to deal with 'impossible' bumps at United States Grand Prix circuit

"I think anyone going to a big event expect traffic, and they expect to wait when they come to a major world-class event like this. But I don't think anyone wants three, and four, or five-hour waits. But if we had sold 25,000 more tickets, we would have run into that. So we stopped.

"And that's our major constraint right now. It's not once they get out here. It's the last mile or so of the highway. So we stopped selling. It's both a good problem to have, and I'd much rather have it that way. I'm not complaining about that. We try to preserve the fan experience, not just while they're on property, but the experience to and from."

The fan experience was an inescapable talking point at COTA this week, with an unmissable new feature in town.

Gondolas and VIPs

Looming over the circuit's iconic first corner was an enormous new addition to the landscape, accessible via six ski-lift gondolas that go up from the paddock, over Turn 1, and back again. It features swimming pools on the roof so that invited guests can watch the racing while submerged in water, while it also boasts corporate hospitality and an almost complete view of the race track.

For some fans, it represented everything wrong with modern Formula 1: a corporate structure for big-money guests. Fans on social media pointed to the famous shot of cars as they round the final corner, with an uninterrupted view all the way up the Turn 1 hill and up to the Texas sky, where a U.S. flag would proudly wave. The new structure was unmissable on TV, as were the gondolas going back and forth, but it should be said, the Big Red grandstand on Turn 1 did not move an inch to accommodate the new building.

Seven-time world champion Hamilton, a long-time fan of Austin's venue and a big advocate of the job Epstein has done in evolving the circuit since its debut, joked that the only thing it had ruined was the previous view of the blue sky as you drove up towards Turn 1. "You just had the clouds and the flag, but you still have the flag," he said, although the flag did have to shift left to accommodate the new building.

Hamilton was unimpressed at the suggestion some fans had been critical of COTA's new feature.

"It's so easy for people to just be always negative about everything. At the end of the day it's an incredible building, the ski lift up to it is pretty phenomenal. What Bobby and his team have done with this track, if you think of the whole place, the fairground, the stage where people perform, it's an unbelievable circuit.

"I think it's one of the best overall circuits, it's super clean, access, getting in, everything. The grandstands, this whole paddock, for me it's one of the best."

McLaren's Oscar Piastri said the only impact it had on him was the first time he drove underneath the gondola, but otherwise had no issue with it.

- Kimi Antonelli wins United States GP but made to wait for first F1 title

- Fernando Alonso lashes out at 'quality of drivers' at bottom of F1 grid

"There's a bit more atmosphere, a bit more going on," Piastri said. "Before you kind of looked at the sky. Now you can see a few more people. The cable cars ... The first lap, I was like, OK, that's pretty close!

"But after that, yeah, I mean, I think it adds to the atmosphere in some ways, so it's not changed much."

It is easy to get bogged down by what a giant new corporate megastructure means for the current state of Formula 1, but it's no coincidence more and more circuits are finding ways to accommodate the growing interest from sponsors, partners and celebrities.

There's a simpler way of looking at it, too: COTA's bumper extension to 2034, the longest contract it's ever been given, was largely rooted in the building of the new facility.

"That's part of the deal," Epstein said, referring to the new Turn 1 unit. "F1 want us to build the building. Well, [we said] give us a long enough commitment so we can benefit from it."

COTA - the best circuit going, or a pain in the back?

The circuit, which debuted in 2012, has always been a favourite of drivers, thanks to its high-speed nature and the way it undulates up and down through the Texan soil. "I always say COTA is, out of all the new-generation tracks, by far the most exciting that has been designed, I think, and the most different," Sainz said ahead of the event. "And I think it's a track that a lot of circuits could take as a good example of, with the kind of design it has for overtaking, the kind of ups and downs, the roller coaster feeling. I think normally we tend to always like good old-school tracks, but Austin, even if it's not an old-school track, it feels like one. I think that's why many drivers like it and enjoy it."

The age of COTA's circuit has created a growing talking point around the event, one likely to be a recurring one as long as the circuit is on the calendar. Driver feedback on the bumpiness was mixed, but Red Bull's Verstappen came into the weekend suggesting he would need a new spine to cope with it.

He later revealed he has seen concerning X-rays showing damage to the discs in his lower back from the wear and tear of racing. In response to comments Epstein made to ESPN that everything bar Turn 1 was fine, and that Verstappen would change his mind after driving on the track again, the Dutchman fired back.

"I invite him to drive my car," Verstappen told Dutch media after qualifying second on Saturday. "I think he'd have to get out after five laps and wouldn't be able to walk anymore."

Not every driver felt the same way.

When told about other driver complaints, Hamilton said. "People are complaining, I'm 42 and my back is fine."

The Ferrari driver added: "It is bumpy, but I think it's OK ... I personally like the bumps, I think it adds character to the track, it feels flat and I love the challenge of that. The car is moving and you have to correct it, in a perfect world it would be a flat track, but then there would be lacking character. I think that's what gives this track that little bit more, it's already a great layout, but the bumps give it a bit more."

stories.headline: Bafana boss Pitso Mosimane's latest South Africa squad shows favouritism fears were unfounded
stories.summary: Mosimane has made several changes from his first preliminary squad, which he announced almost immediately after taking charge at the beginning of September.
stories.body:
When Pitso Mosimane returned as Bafana Bafana head coach, sceptics feared that his proximity to South African club football would lead to an erosion of the meritocratic culture Hugo Broos had built, but the 62-year-old's second preliminary squad suggests it has only been enhanced.

Mosimane began his tenure with Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) qualifying wins over Guinea and Eritrea and a friendly victory over Egypt. Next up is the AFCON qualifying double-header against Kenya on Nov. 13 & 17.

Mosimane has made several changes from his first preliminary squad, which he announced almost immediately after taking charge at the beginning of September.

Chicago Fire's Mbekezeli Mbokazi has returned from injury, while Aden McCarthy, Botiumelo Radiopane, Nqaba Xulu, Luke le Roux, Thalente Mbatha, Nkosikhona Radebe, Devin Titus and Thakasani Mbanjwa have also received call-ups.

For every one of these call-ups, a layman can deduce a clear possible motive. McCarthy is the most obvious among them -- he has consistently featured at centre-back for Sabah in the UEFA Champions League and performed well at the highest level.

Radiopane and Xulu are in hot scoring form domestically for Orlando Pirates and Richards Bay respectively. Titus has earned his place with a strong start to life at MAS Fes in Morocco. Mbatha is back from injury and le Roux on the books of a new club at Cercle Brugge after struggling for game time at Portsmouth.

Radebe adds a right-back option from an in-form AmaZulu side with Mamelodi Sundowns' Khuliso Mudau still on the mend from injury. Mbanjwa is rewarded for a strong start to the season in goal for Golden Arrows.

Yanela Mbuthuma and Shandre Campbell -- both of whom have experienced dips in form and fortune at club level since the last international break -- are notable absentees.

In cutting two players he had given opportunities to after they had been mostly overlooked by Broos, Mosimane suggested he is willing to operate without fear or favour.

When 'Jingles' was on the verge of being appointed, Broos was quoted as telling Het Nieuwsblad: "You know, South Africa still don't have a coach. The candidate is Pitso Mosimane, a successful South African coach.

"But they know that if he comes in, they'll go five years back in time. Club owners and agents calling coaches to influence the squad selection. I threw all of them out. If one called, I would say bluntly: 'I don't talk with agents'."

The concern over agents and owners trying their luck in influencing the Bafana head coach may have been well-founded. Broos was not the first to complain of this within the national team setup.

However, questioning if Mosimane himself was open to influence without proof he was willing to make publicly available was ill-advised. It is impossible to accurately speculate on what conversations have or have not gone on between Mosimane and club owners and agents in the two months since then, but what is clear is that his team selection has been thoroughly meritocratic.

The momentum he has garnered is reminiscent of what Broos achieved in the first six months of his tenure.

At the time, the Belgian's irreverent team selection and approach to squad culture put everybody on their toes and led to an uptick in results. After they had failed to qualify for AFCON 2021 immediately before Broos was appointed, the Belgian fell narrowly short of steering Bafana into qualification playoffs for the 2022 World Cup.

In subsequent years, he kicked on and led Bafana to third place at AFCON 2023 (held belatedly in Ivory Coast in early 2024) and the 2026 World Cup round of 32.

When discussing the most successful Bafana Bafana coaches of all-time, Broos should be placed alongside Clive Barker in the top two. However, even the brightest tacticians eventually settle on patterns in their squad selection, and towards the end of his tenure, the Belgian became more predictable in certain aspects.

There was a fairly settled back five of Ronwen Williams, Aubrey Modiba, Mbokazi, Ime Okon and Mudau, and until he switched up his attacking plan to revive the FIFA World Cup campaign, Broos was likely to start Lyle Foster upfront with Evidence Makgopa the main alternative.

In midfield, Teboho Mokoena was a near certain starter and Sphephelo Sithole the clear preferred option alongside him, although Broos occasionally tinkered with his formation and left room for the likes of Bathusi Aubaas and the late Jayden Adams in the holding role. Nkosinathi Sibisi was considered another option, occasionally stepping out from the back into midfield.

Mosimane's arrival has reopened competition for places in these positions. Brooklyn Poggenpoel is retained in the squad after impressing in midfield over the last international break.

After Mbuthuma's minutes upfront, Radiopane and Xulu have been given a chance to earn theirs. Foster has made a second successive preliminary squad, although he failed to make the final squad last time out while in the process of leaving Burnley on loan to Houston Dynamo and settling in.

Fawaaz Basadien, Olwethu Makhanya, and McCarthy are in consideration in the backline. Mudau is, however, still the likely first-choice at right-back for the time being when he returns to full fitness. Still, Mosimane has done well to identify alternatives.

Mosimane declined to get drawn into a war of words with Broos over anything not directly related to matters on the pitch and instead praised his predecessor's impressive record as Bafana head coach.

In his first stint, Mosimane may not have succeeded in the hotseat. However, early results and his approach to team selection suggest he has justified the decision of the South African Football Association (SAFA) to give him a second chance and trust him to navigate the role without fear or favour to anyone.

stories.headline: WNBA Finals odds: Valkyries flip the odds with Game 5 win over Dream
stories.summary: After falling to +225, Golden State has rattled off back-to-back wins to become the -260 favorite to win the WNBA Finals.
stories.body:
After going down 2-1 and falling to as long as +225 to win the 2026 WNBA Finals, the Golden State Valkyries have stormed back with two straight victories and are now -260 favorites for their first title. The Atlanta Dream, who entered Monday's Game 5 as the slight -115 favorites for the championship, are now +215 underdogs.

Atlanta began the campaign with solid +650 odds to win the Finals, fourth on the odds board, but Golden State came in at a much longer 45-1, ninth on the board, in just its second season of existence.

Roughly in line with the series odds, Gabby Williams is the overwhelming -210 favorite for Finals MVP, and Angel Reese (+275) leads the way for the Dream should they make a comeback. Kiah Stokes (15-1) and Veronica Burton (18-1) both hold outside shots at the honor, according to the betting lines.

The series returns to Atlanta for a Thursday matinee Game 6 with the Dream 3.5-point favorites. The over/under comes in at 147.5 after Monday's contest recorded just 119 points.

stories.headline: NBA buzz: Latest on trades, news, roster moves and intel
stories.summary: The NBA is back. The buzz never left. Bookmark this page for the latest news, rumblings and analysis from ESPN's insiders.
stories.body:
The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops.

The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks. The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics, and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season.

Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season?

All season long, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders.

Quick links:

Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Oct. 27

What Edwards' injury means for Wolves

On Monday, Anthony Edwards looked like an MVP candidate as he poured in 47 points in Cleveland; on Tuesday, that dream was dashed early, as ESPN's Shams Charania reported that Edwards will miss up to two months due to knee surgery.

Minnesota can still contend this season, as long as Edwards returns healthy at the end of that projected time frame. The partnership of Edwards and LaMelo Ball was one of the most exciting elements of the new season, and the Timberwolves had raced to a 3-1 start featuring three blowout wins, with only an overtime loss to the Cavaliers marring their ledger. At the end of two more months, they will still have 52 games remaining on their schedule.

But they won't be comfortable in the meantime. The Timberwolves have a relatively shallow roster, and their bench will be stretched very thin once sixth man Ayo Dosunmu moves into the starting lineup to replace Edwards. Their two-way star's absence also reduces any margin for error with the rest of the roster; Ball is notoriously injury-prone, and if both guards are ever out at the same time, a lengthy losing streak could ensue.

Edwards to undergo surgery, miss up to two months

Minnesota Timberwolves star Anthony Edwards will undergo an arthroscopic procedure on his ailing right knee that will sideline him for up to two months, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Edwards has been on the injury report for the injury. He dealt with runner's knee in the same leg last season.

Leonard out multiple weeks, misses return to LA

Toronto Raptors forward Kawhi Leonard will miss multiple weeks due to left knee swelling, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. An MRI showed no structural damage, but the recovery will keep Leonard out of a return game at the LA Clippers on Monday, Nov. 2.

Read more: NBA punishes Clippers after Kawhi investigation: Top questions

Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to discuss the NBA's first week, including the early message the San Antonio Spurs sent, the Houston Rockets rising to be potential contenders and an 0-3 start for the Miami Heat. "They'll replace him with what they have on their roster with Ajay Mitchell. He becomes a very important piece right now and the fact that they had to trade away multiple wings over the summer -- Aaron Wiggins and Lu Dort ... It comes into play for sure, but this means Ajay Mitchell will have to have a big season and now Cason Wallace, who was just rewarded with a huge contract, those guys will be needed. And you also could see some opportunities for Bennett Stirtz, who actually I think got his first NBA basket tonight. The last weekend of the offseason is expected to bring a flurry of transactions.

Bronny on LeBron James' Lakers exit: 'He's got his own path'

When LeBron James chose to leave the Los Angeles Lakers in free agency over the summer, he consulted his family on the decision to sign with the Philadelphia 76ers. But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid.

"We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. So it wasn't really much [discussion] to be honest with you," Bronny James said Monday at Lakers media day.

"He's got his own path and I got my own. He knows that I want to make a name for myself and I want to continue my career and keep growing as a player. And he knows that I want to focus on that. So he decided to do that."

LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets. Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase its projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. They will be free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The 2023 first-round pick is eligible until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grading the Curry deal: Why Warriors don't get an A

Hornets star Knueppel sidelined by hamstring injury
The Charlotte Hornets announced that Kon Knueppel will be out for at least the entire preseason because of a left hamstring injury.

James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers
LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July.

"[Embiid has] done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," James said. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

Grizzlies waive Russell
The Memphis Grizzlies have waived D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

stories.headline: World Series down only 6% amid low ratings predictions
stories.summary: For those fearing record-low ratings for the World Series, the matchup between the Brewers and Rays is exceeding expectations.
stories.body:
For those fearing record-low ratings for the World Series, the matchup between the Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays is exceeding expectations.

The audiences for the first two games on Fox Sports were down only 6% compared to Games 1 and 2 from last year's Fall Classic between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Toronto Blue Jays.

"I think they've probably surpassed everybody's expectations. I think very few people, including me, would've guessed that we'd be down 6% through two games. We're really satisfied," said Mike Mulvihill, Fox Sports president for insight and analytics.

Milwaukee's 3-2 win in Game 1 last Friday averaged 12.26 million viewers on Fox, Fox Deportes, Fox One streaming, the Fox Sports app and Univision. The Brewers' 5-4 victory in Game 2, which did not include Univision coverage, averaged 10.85 million.

Both games were the most-watched broadcast of the night.

With two small-market teams vying for the championship, there were many predictions the early ratings could rival the 2023 World Series between the Texas Rangers and Arizona Diamondbacks, which was the least-watched on record with a 9.11 million average. Game 2 of that series set the record low at 8.15 million.

The difference this year, though, is that Milwaukee has a steady base of fans in the Midwest and has been a consistent contender the past couple of seasons. This is also a matchup of the two teams with the best records in baseball this season.

"I do think there's something helpful about having a traditional team from the Midwest in the series. And the fact that they were able to take down the two-time defending champs (the Dodgers) and do it in really convincing fashion, I think that helps build some interest for the World Series," Mulvihill said.

The Fox-only average for the first two games this year is 11.05 million.

Fox could be holding its breath for the ratings from Monday's Game 3. Not only was it a 10-1 blowout win for Milwaukee, it faced stiff competition with the Dallas Cowboys playing the Philadelphia Eagles on "Monday Night Football."

stories.headline: Buckner, Nelson trades signal Colts' rebuild underway
stories.summary: DeForest Buckner and Quenton Nelson are headed to contending teams. Could Jonathan Taylor be next?
stories.body:
INDIANAPOLIS -- DeForest Buckner had seen enough.

As the curtains closed Sunday on the Indianapolis Colts' third straight loss, punctuating a season that began with high hopes and devolved into a road to nowhere, the veteran defensive tackle finally let his emotions show.

Asked by a reporter how he felt after losing to the Minnesota Vikings to fall to 2-5, the three-time Pro Bowl selection was blunt.

"I don't know, how 'bout you guess," he said. "I'm frustrated. Same thing. We lost."

The losing wore on Buckner. But he and fellow Colts standout Quenton Nelson, an All-Pro guard, will no longer have to endure the frustration. Both were traded Tuesday during one of the most consequential days for the franchise since the stunning 2019 retirement of quarterback Andrew Luck.

But this development was much easier to predict than Luck's departure as it follows the firing of general manager Chris Ballard last week.

Assistant general manager Ed Dodds engineered Tuesday's deals, presumably at the direction of owner Carlie Irsay-Gordon. Buckner is heading back to the San Francisco 49ers, the team that drafted him and traded him to Indianapolis in 2020. Nelson is headed to the Seattle Seahawks, one of the Niners' main NFC West rivals. Both players were in the final year of their contracts and their futures in Indianapolis were uncertain at best.

Moves such as these appeared likely following Ballard's dismissal in his 10th season on the job. Ballard and the Colts had tried tweaking the roster to varying degrees in recent years. And they have tried every iteration of quarterback acquisition in their efforts to replace Luck.

In the end, it all amounted to nothing.

The Colts have not won the AFC South since 2014. They last made the playoffs in 2020. Their last postseason victory came in 2018. They've averaged 7.6 wins over the past five seasons. Even great players such as Buckner and Nelson weren't enough to overcome the club's other shortcomings.

Tuesday's difficult decisions made it official: The Colts are done with that chapter.

The next phase of franchise history will be a full rebuild. The Colts must embark on that rebuild without a first-round pick in 2027 as that selection is heading to the New York Jets to complete last year's Sauce Gardner trade. So, Tuesday's moves were a step toward rebuilding the draft capital that the team's next top executive will need to begin what will be a difficult job.

The Colts are expected to entertain additional deals with players such as running back Jonathan Taylor, nose tackle Grover Stewart and receiver Josh Downs attracting interest from other clubs.

But for now, Indianapolis has a single second-round pick in 2027, two third-round choices and two fourth-round selections among its selections. The Nelson deal garnered a 2027 third-round choice (along with a 2028 fifth-rounder) from Seattle, and Buckner netted a 2027 fourth-round choice from San Francisco.

In terms of free agency, the Colts are projected to have well north of $60 million in salary cap space next spring. They could create significantly more if they trade Taylor or move on from struggling quarterback Daniel Jones.

Roster flexibility isn't likely to be an issue for the next regime in Indianapolis. But getting to that point is sure to be painful.

Kind of like Tuesday.

stories.headline: Nowhere to rise for Volkanovski and Yan, but Reyes and Volkov move up
stories.summary: Here's a look at every weight class to determine the best of the best in UFC, PFL and beyond.
stories.body:
Two of the greatest performances at UFC 333 earned no reward in ESPN's divisional MMA rankings.

Both featherweight champion Alexander Volkanovski, who knocked out Movsar Evloev in Saturday's main event, and men's bantamweight titlist Petr Yan, who won a trilogy fight against Merab Dvalishvili in the co-main, were already ranked No. 1 in their divisions, so there was nowhere for them to rise in those top 10s.

Evloev, who lost for the first time in his career, and Dvalishvili, an ex-champ who dropped his second straight to Yan, maintain their No. 2 rankings.

Other fights on the Abu Dhabi card did affect rankings. Light heavyweight Dominick Reyes was the lone fighter to defeat someone ranked higher than him, knocking out sixth-ranked light heavyweight Azamat Murzakanov. Reyes moves from No. 7 to the top five, and Murzakanov falls to Reyes' former spot.

Heavyweight saw a trickle-down succession of movement, partly due to a fight result. Alexander Volkov, who beat unranked Rizvan Kuniev, moves up one position to No. 3, largely because former UFC champion Tom Aspinall, previously ranked second, has been removed from the top 10 as ineligible because he has not fought in over a year. The other ranked heavyweights each move up one spot, and Kuniev enters the rankings at No. 10.

The other ranking change is at men's flyweight, where Lone'er Kavanagh climbs one position to No. 6 after handing unranked Ramazan Temirov his first loss.
